articles.headline: Carmelo Anthony thinks Knicks right to halt contract talks to focus on season
articles.description: Former Knicks great Carmelo Anthony said the team is making the right decision in halting contract negotiations with players to focus solely on basketball.
articles.headlineJa: カーメロ・アンソニー、ニックスがシーズンに集中するため契約交渉を中断した判断を支持
articles.descriptionJa: 元ニックスのスター選手であるカーメロ・アンソニーは、バスケットボールに専念するために選手との契約交渉を中断するというチームの決定は正しいと述べた。
articles.body:
STAMFORD, Conn. -- Carmelo Anthony believes the New York Knicks made the right decision in halting contract negotiations with some of their players to focus solely on basketball.

With Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart eligible for extensions but talks going nowhere, the Knicks said last week they were pausing discussions until later in the season and would devote their attention entirely to defending their NBA championship.

Anthony, an All-Star for the Knicks during his Hall of Fame career, said Monday he wasn't alarmed by what he was hearing from a team that should be enjoying happy times.

"I think it's happier times, I just think things just move so fast now that you get a chance to celebrate the championship, then it's business as usual, right? Business has got to go on," Anthony said.

 

"I think it was big for them to stop the conversations, and just, we'll get to that. We'll get to that at the end of the season."

Anthony spoke at NBC Sports studios, where he is preparing for his second season as an analyst for the network's "NBA Showtime" studio show. 

Towns is eligible for a four-year, $276 million deal. He is due to make $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for 2027-28.

He has been disappointed in the progress of talks after being an All-Star in both seasons since coming to New York and told reporters that the Knicks' statement Friday that they were cutting off negotiations "was news to me."

Hart will make $21 million this season and the Knicks have an option for 2027-28 at $22.4 million. He said he wasn't frustrated but had previously noted what it could mean for players at the trade deadline in February if there hadn't been progress on contract talks. 

Anthony was represented by Leon Rose, who is now the Knicks president, when he was traded to New York in 2011. A frequent spectator during the team's title run, he believes the players and management will be able to work things out respectfully.

"But whatever's going to happen is going to happen," Anthony said. "But right now, let the be all be the be all, which is basketball. Let's go defend this championship. And I think both parties understand."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: NFL Week 5 arrivals: Ravens trio channels early 2000s style ahead of 'SNF'
articles.description: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第5週の到着シーン：レイブンズの3人が「SNF」を前に2000年代初頭のスタイルを披露
articles.descriptionJa: NFLのスター選手たちは、試合当日のスタジアム到着シーンを毎週のファッションショーへと変え続けている。
articles.body:
Week 5 of the NFL season is here, and October is starting to bring a little more variety to the forecast -- and potentially to pregame fashion.

With fall temperatures settling into parts of the country and lingering heat beginning to ease elsewhere, players have another opportunity to switch up their game-day looks. 

California's early-October heat wave has weakened, while cooler conditions in the Northeast and a hurricane that brought heavy rain to parts of the South made for a mixed bag across the country this weekend. That leaves room for everything from lightweight fits to layered looks as players make their stadium entrances.

Whether they're embracing the season with jackets and sweaters or sticking to their signature styles, NFL players are bringing another round of personality to the tunnel in Week 5.

Monday night style

Monday evenings in Los Angeles call for comfort wear, especially with temperatures in the mid-60s. Such was the case for the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams. But comfort wear is where players and able to showcase their creativity and style. Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald did just that with a monochromatic matching set.

Primetime fashion

 The Baltimore Ravens turned back the clock with some early 2000s-inspired fashion ahead of their Sunday Night Football matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. Cornerbacks Chandler Rivers and Keyon Martin joined safety Keondre Jackson in rocking backwards throwback basketball jerseys, oversized shorts and nostalgic accessories. Rivers led the way in a blue Derrick Rose Memphis Tigers jersey, baggy denim shorts and wheat Timberland boots, while Martin sported Penny Hardaway's pinstriped Orlando Magic jersey and Jackson repped Carmelo Anthony and the New York Knicks. The coordinated looks brought a dose of Y2K nostalgia to the Ravens' arrival in Atlanta.

Sunday's best

Throwback jerseys honoring New England sports legends were a theme ahead of Sunday's matchup between the Las Vegas Raiders and New England Patriots. Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby arrived in a Larry Bird jersey, while Patriots safety Craig Woodson sported a Ty Law jersey as New England prepared to celebrate the 25th anniversary of its Super Bowl XXXVI championship. 

Thursday night drip

Dallas Cowboys teammates Cooper Beebe and Brevyn Spann-Ford showed some love to the Dallas Stars ahead of "Thursday Night Football." Beebe arrived in a Jake Oettinger jersey, while Spann-Ford repped Stars legend Mike Modano.

articles.headline: LaFleur: 1-4 Cardinals not planning to change playcallers
articles.description: Mike LaFleur says he does not plan on making changes to any of Arizona's coaching duties after a 1-4 start.
articles.headlineJa: ラフルコーチ、1勝4敗のカージナルスはプレーコール担当の変更を予定せず
articles.descriptionJa: マイク・ラフルは、1勝4敗という出だしの後でも、アリゾナのコーチ陣の役割を変更する計画はないと述べた。
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur says he does not plan on making changes to any of the team's coaching duties after a 1-4 start.

LaFleur said Monday, in the wake of a 45-21 loss to the Detroit Lions, that he will not replace himself as the offensive playcaller or defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, who calls the defensive plays.

"I mean, obviously my job is to see the issues and handle the issues and have the tough conversations," LaFleur said. "So, if I felt like changes were needed for us to help us win this week, then I'm going to do that. It's my responsibility, but I don't think that gives us the best chance to win this week.

"I think the best thing to do right now is reevaluate what we've done, what we've done well, because there are some bright spots, but there's also a lot of spots that we got to improve on. And I told the defense when I talked to the defense today where our changes are going to be made; again, I'll keep that in-house, and I'm fired up to see it happen."

One potential change this week could be in how the Cardinals structure their active roster on game day Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams.

LaFleur said Arizona will have a discussion Tuesday to talk about putting rookie quarterback Carson Beck on the active roster instead of him being the inactive emergency quarterback. The Cardinals had not had those discussions yet this season, LaFleur said, but added that they would consider it "if we think that's what's best."

LaFleur said he had "some tough conversations" with all three phases Monday about where he thinks they can improve. He singled out the offense and defense for needing to find ways to improve.

LaFleur said he watched film of the offense first, then the defense, followed by special teams, and then "just started having conversations" centered around one foundational question: "How do we not allow this to happen ever again?"

Answering that has proved to be easier said than done for the Cardinals, whose defense has allowed more than 30 points in each of the past four games, all losses.

LaFleur expressed confidence in his defensive players Monday, saying he has the "right guys on defense to play better" because he has seen glimpses of it at times in the first five weeks. Arizona has seven sacks in its past two games, its best two-game stretch since Weeks 12 and 13 of the 2024 season, when they had 10 in two games.

The issue, LaFleur said, is that he hasn't seen the defensive production consistently.

"I told them that today, but we got to help them with that, whether that's providing the clarity, whether it's making it easier, what have you," LaFleur said. "And we got to dive into that hard over these next two days.

"And same thing on offense. When it's going good, it's going good, or it's a three-and-out machine, and there's really nowhere in between right now for us. So, we got to figure out how to do all the good stuff better and then obviously clean up those three-and-outs."

DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Moore is out for Monday Night Football against the Rams. It is his first time missing a game due to injury since 2020. That leaves Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Skyler Bell and called up from the practice squad, Trent Sherfield as the Bills receivers with Joshua Palmer also out this week. I would prefer to play Coleman of the bunch as he brings more upside. Coleman has been the Bills most productive receiver when Moore's missed time. articles.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley says he's not mulling QB change entering bye
articles.description: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley is not considering a quarterback change heading into their Week 6 bye, but he did say the passing offense must improve.
articles.headlineJa: ドルフィンズのジェフ・ハフレイ監督、バイウィーク前にQB変更は検討していないと明言
articles.descriptionJa: ドルフィンズのジェフ・ハフレイ監督は、第6週のバイウィーク（休み週）を前にクォーターバックの変更は考えていないとしているが、パス攻撃の改善は必須であると述べた。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley is not considering a quarterback change heading into their Week 6 bye, but he did say his team's passing offense must improve.

Speaking to reporters Monday, Hafley reiterated that Malik Willis will remain the team's starting quarterback, and he is not considering a change to backup Kyle McCord. However, particularly after Sunday's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, during which the Dolphins struggled to move the ball through the air, Hafley acknowledged the team must be able to pass the ball more effectively.

"Malik needs to be better, OK? And that's not the headline," Hafley said. "The headline is we all need to be better, and I mean that. I thought yesterday for the first time we ran the ball really well and we moved the ball. We ran for 200 yards against a really good team. But everything in the pass game has to be better, right? It's the receivers, it's the tight ends, it's the protection. It all has to tie in, and it all has to be better.

"And that's the quarterback, that's the coaches, that's the offensive line, that's the running backs, that's the tight ends. This is a team game that we all need to be more efficient, and we need to be better. And we will work through that. I have confidence in the coaches, I have confidence in the players that we have. We will work through that and we will get better. It's been five weeks."

Willis ranks 31st in the NFL with a 56.2% completion percentage and 23rd in quarterback rating (43.9). Through five games, he has thrown for 849 yards and two touchdowns against four interceptions.

The onetime third-round pick has also rushed for 186 yards and two touchdowns, albeit with five fumbles.

Willis has lost fumbles in each of his past three games, which is an area Hafley said the team will focus on during the bye week.

"We got to look hard at it during the bye week," Hafley said. "We talk about ball security all the time and we work on it and we've got to do a better job of putting him in those situations and he's got to have the awareness to protect the ball as well. We'll take a hard look at fixing that because we're not going to win games if we're fumbling the ball like that."

The Dolphins' offense is the youngest in the NFL, with three rookies receiving consistent playing time. Their offensive line, which returned its top four starters from a season ago, ranks middle of the pack in terms of protection with a 50.8% pass block win rate. But Willis is the fifth-most contacted quarterback in the league, and the fourth-most sacked.

He got off to a slow start in Sunday's loss, at one point throwing more interceptions than completions before ultimately finishing with 137 yards and a touchdown on 15-of-27 passing.

Miami enters its bye week on a five-game losing streak to start the season and Willis said the week needs to focus on self-reflection and accountability if the team is to earn its first win since Dec. 28.

articles.headline: Lampard: Coventry 'feet on the ground' after Newcastle win
articles.description: Coventry City boss Frank Lampard is not allowing his side to get carried away after they earned a thumping 4-1 home victory over Newcastle United on Monday.
articles.body:
Coventry City boss Frank Lampard is not allowing his side to get carried away after they earned a thumping 4-1 home victory over Newcastle United on Monday.

Jack Rudoni tucked away a sixth-minute penalty after Lukás Hornícek brought down Sidiki Cherif inside the area which gave the hosts a halftime lead.

The Sky Blues made a quick start to the second period as well, and Cherif doubled their lead before Sven Botman's belter halved the deficit with 20 minutes to go -- making for a nervous atmosphere

But Coventry were able to wrap up their first home Premier League win in 25 years courtesy of further efforts from Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni, and make it back-to-back wins for Lampard's newly promoted men.

Lampard, whose side moved up to 14th in the table with the win, was over the moon with his side's performance, but wants them to stay grounded with another "tough" challenge against Tottenham on the horizon.

He said: "We are going to be a relative underdog in pretty much every game, so we have to maximise everything beyond the limit. It's a good feeling for the players.

"They need to keep their feet on the ground because the next one is tough and the one after that is tough. We looked like a team that was hard for teams to come here (and beat) tonight. That's the feeling we haven't had in our first home games this season.

"This gives good confidence, so it's a balance of confidence against over-confidence for us.

"They have to stay humble to that and understand. Every part of the level has gone up."

Coventry failed to score in their first four league matches, but it seems Lampard's side have now broken the shackles after netting five times in their last couple of outings.

Four different players got on the scoresheet, a pleasing sign for Lampard who saw his team finish highest scorers in the Championship last season.

He added: "It's not a nice feeling, looking at the table and seeing zero goals before Forest.

"Your left-back who hardly scores [Jay Dasilva], scores at Forest, it's a lovely story but we need more. It's great and I think it'll be great for lads going forward to feel that confidence.

"Good for all the players that scored and good for the team to feel that we can rely on that."

Another 4-1 defeat for Newcastle means they have now conceded the joint most goals in the league so far alongside Bournemouth and Chelsea.

Boss Matthias Jaissle made it clear that the result was not acceptable, but feels they were better than when they lost by the same scoreline to Leeds a month ago.

He said: "I think it was a tough story throughout the whole match. There were elements in both boxes where we need to step up and improve.

"It's not something we can compare with the Leeds match today because I think we were at least better.

"The goals we conceded, it was a different story. We were better after the first 10 minutes, we dominated the game but conceded easy goals, which we need to improve.

articles.headline: Commanders' Quinn says 'no one is pleased' after botched play fuels fan angst
articles.description: Commanders coach Dann Quinn explained the breakdown that caused a botched final play in Sunday's overtime tie, saying it's ultimately his responsibility.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn met with team owner Josh Harris, as he regularly does, after Sunday's overtime tie with the Giants and said Monday that no one is happy with the game's botched final sequence or the team's 1-3-1 record.

And while Quinn declined to say if he was now worried about his job security, he did say, "I do know how the league goes. I'm well aware of that."

"Trust me, no one is pleased with this outcome and where we're at," Quinn said after his latest meeting with Harris. "But we do have those hard conversations, we're honest about what we're at and what we need to fix and what we need to work on. And so I like having that communication with him."

There are no plans to make any coaching changes, a team source with knowledge of the situation told ESPN. But this start preceded by a 5-12 season has led to such questions only two years after Quinn guided the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game.

Those questions were fueled by what happened at the end of overtime Sunday, when Washington reached the Giants' 24-yard line with 50 seconds remaining and the score tied. The offense did not end up snapping the ball for the next play until 12 seconds remained. With no timeouts left, quarterback Jayden Daniels dropped back to pass after a fake handoff, then started to scramble and was tackled with eight seconds to play.

As Commanders players half-heartedly got back to the line, with Daniels and others slow to get off the ground, Washington ran out of time to spike the ball and stop the clock to set up a game-winning field goal attempt.

Quinn said offensive coordinator David Blough called the play, but he is ultimately responsible for what transpires.

"All of that comes through me," Quinn said. "Dave's the one that calls it, but I want to make sure I'm clear on my guidelines, too. This will break down in a lot of ways, so it starts with me first."

The Commanders do have a game management coordinator in the booth, Connor Nickol, to help. But the issue, Quinn said, was the team trying to do too much. The previous play ended at 50 seconds, but the Commanders subbed in players and did not line up for the next snap until 18 seconds remained -- and the ball wasn't snapped for another six seconds.

"It took entirely too long to execute our strategy," Quinn said, "from subbing to clock awareness to clocking the ball."

Quinn said "burning some time is the smart call" in that situation because three field goals and an extra point had been missed in the game. The Commanders did not want to give New York much time on the clock in a worst-case scenario if they missed a field goal.

Washington then ran a play-action pass with three tight ends and a receiver -- two of them ended up 14 yards downfield.

Quinn said if it hadn't taken so long to run the next play, then, "you can get back on the ball and clock it. ... Hindsight, don't sub, we can get back on the ball with the same group and do the same outcome."

articles.headline: Kristaps Porzingis expected to be at Warriors' facility on Tuesday
articles.description: Veteran center Kristaps Porzingis is expected to return to the Golden State Warriors practice facility Tuesday afternoon, according to head coach Steve Kerr.
articles.body:
Veteran center Kristaps Porzingis is expected to return to the Golden State Warriors practice facility Tuesday afternoon, according to coach Steve Kerr.

Porzingis has been away from the Warriors for the first two weeks of preseason while attending to what the team is deeming a private "health issue."

It's not immediately clear when the Warriors anticipate Porzingis will return to the court. They will be in Las Vegas for a preseason game Tuesday when Porzingis is expected to arrive at the team's San Francisco facility and meet with Rick Celebrini, its lead medical decision-maker.

Two seasons ago, Porzingis contracted an upper respiratory virus while playing for the Boston Celtics, and he has since vaguely revealed the lingering impact it has had on his health and ability to consistently play NBA basketball.

Porzingis was limited to 34 games last season, split between the Atlanta Hawks and the Warriors, who traded Jonathan Kuminga for him in February. They then re-signed Porzingis to a two-year, $40 million deal this summer.

The contract was structured strategically to allow the Warriors to trade Porzingis at any point and limit their long-term downside. Only $3 million of the $20 million next season is guaranteed.

Porzingis has been in regular contact with Celebrini and the Warriors' front office the past two weeks while on an indefinite absence, while the front office has told Kerr and the team to focus on the season rather than deal with Porzingis' unclear availability.

In his absence, Kerr said he is leaning toward starting a smaller lineup of Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green.

articles.headline: Coventry put four past Newcastle to climb out of relegation zone
articles.description: Coventry City picked up their first home victory in the Premier League for 25 years with an emphatic 4-1 win over Newcastle United on Monday.
articles.body:
Coventry City picked up their first home victory in the Premier League for 25 years with an emphatic 4-1 win over Newcastle United on Monday.

The last time Newcastle played on a Monday night they were hammered 4-1 by Leeds and suffered the same miserable fate in Coventry less than a month later.

Jack Rudoni's sixth-minute penalty gave Frank Lampard's side a dream start and their first Premier League goal in front of their own fans since John Hartson scored in a 1-0 win over Sunderland in April 2001.

It was the first time Coventry fans had seen a Premier League goal at the Coventry Building Society Arena with their last goal in the top flight coming at Highfield Road.

Bobby Thomas' last-man clearance left Matias Fernandez-Pardo waiting for his first goal for the club and that proved to be vital as Sidiki Cherif doubled the hosts lead three minutes into the second period.

Newcastle got themselves back in the contest through a belter from Sven Botman after 70 minutes but Coventry were not to be denied as Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni ensured they moved out of the drop zone with successive wins to draw level on points with Manchester United on a memorable night.

Newcastle started sloppily which set the tone for their disappointing evening, and it led to goalkeeper Lukás Hornícek giving away a penalty in the fourth minute.

The Czech goalkeeper spilled Brandon Thomas-Asante's routine ball and then brought down Cherif before Rudoni calmly sent him the wrong way from 12 yards.

The visitors settled and looked to respond, winger Harvey Barnes looked lively and collected a pass from Joe Willock before firing straight at Carl Rushworth for their first shot on target.

The Sky Blues had a glorious chance to make it two with their first touch inside Newcastle's box since the goal.

Jacob Murphy's cross was cleared by Milan van Ewijk which set Cherif on the counter attack and beyond a high Magpies line but he could only aim straight at Hornicek.

Newcastle should have been on level terms a couple of minutes before the break when Fernandez-Pardo got in behind the Coventry defence from a long clearance, he rounded Rushworth only to see his goalbound effort blocked on the line by the covering Thomas.

Coventry caught Newcastle cold at the start of the second period too as they doubled their advantage.

A long throw into the box was headed out by Malick Thiaw but only into the path of Cherif who arrowed low and hard through several Newcastle bodies and into the bottom right corner.

The Magpies needed something special to get themselves back in the contest and it came when Botman lined one up on the left edge of the area with a bullet too fast for Rushworth to halve the deficit.

The momentum seemingly swung by the way of the visitors but Coventry somehow managed to restore their two-goal lead.

Thomas-Asante dispossessed Joelinton outside his own box and the ball dropped to Simms who saw his effort deflect off Thiaw and in to make it three after 81 minutes

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye move for Fulham youngster King
articles.description: Manchester United are reportedly interested in Fulham teenager Josh King. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Manchester United are interested in Fulham teenager Josh King, while Liverpool are looking at Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are watching the situation of Fulham attacker Josh King after being informed that he could be signed for £50 million, according to Football Insider. The 19-year-old is open to the potential of a switch to Old Trafford, but a deal is expected to be more feasible next summer than in January. Multiple clubs in Europe are also looking at King, who has scored two goals in six Premier League matches so far this season.

- Liverpool see Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis as a potential long-term successor to Alisson Becker, The Sun reports. Tzolakis, 23, has been a standout in the Premier League this season, and Hull are expected to enter talks next month with several suitors keeping tabs on his situation. Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with interest in his signature, with recent reports indicating that his transfer would be valued at £40m.

- Real Madrid are exploring the transfer market for a midfielder as they also prepare to enter contract talks with Jude Bellingham, according to according to Fabrizio Romano. Madrid are keen to find a midfield anchor after missing out on Rodri following his switch to Barcelona in the summer, but they are first prioritizing signing their core players to new deals, with hopes of signing Bellingham, 23, to a two-year extension that will secure his future at the club until the summer of 2031.

- Arsenal are closing in on signing midfielders Declan Rice and Martin Ødegaard to new contracts, while talks are also ongoing with defender Jurriën Timber, TEAMtalk reports. Arsenal are focusing on securing key players to new deals in the coming weeks after making "significant progress," and they are optimistic of confirming all three extensions before January. Rice, 27, and Ødegaard, 27, have both made six Premier League starts this season, while 25-year-old Timber returned from injury last month in the 2-0 league win over Sunderland.

- Liverpool are weighing up their options at right back amid concerns over Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley, with a move for a replacement being considered for the winter transfer window, Football Insider reports. Frimpong, 25, hasn't started a game in the Premier League since August after losing his starting place in the team to Ronald Araújo, while Bradley, 23, is continuing a long return to fitness from a knee injury sustained against Arsenal in January. Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, who has recently been linked with Chelsea, is one of the names on the Reds' shortlist.
